title: GET /api/stocks/{ticker}/history follow-ups — further non-blocking review follow-up
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's review of PR #41 (api-stocks-history-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so it isn't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: In backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py, the new `_RangeOutOfBoundsError` class is defined between `get_history` (which references it in a `try/except` at line ~113, above the class's own definition) and `_trim_to_range` (which raises it, below the definition). This works correctly at runtime -- both functions only touch the name when called, by which point the whole module (including the class statement) has already executed -- but the physical ordering (used-before-defined, then defined-before-raised) is a minor readability wrinkle compared to the codebase's usual pattern of defining an exception type before its first use. Worth moving `_RangeOutOfBoundsError`'s definition up (e.g. directly above `_trim_to_range`, or near the top of the module alongside `_RANGE_PATTERN`) next time this file is touched, purely for readability -- not a functional issue.
